newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian "living wage" claim sensible - RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian "living wage" claim sensible - RBA.

text.p: The Australian government's "Living Wage" claim proposal is sensible, but more interventions may have their costs, said Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane.
"Continuation of such safety net adjustments, as proposed by the Government, seems sensible to us," Macfarlane said in an address to the Committee for the Economic Development of Australia (CEDA).

"But if the interventions are more wide-ranging, the outcome will be slower employment growth - either because individual employers respond to the price/wage squeeze facing them, or because the Bank is forced to respond to emerging inflationary pressures by raising interest rates," he said.
The government is proposing a A$24 per week wage rise for lower paid workers spread over three years.
"With the painful experience of reducing inflation still fresh in our minds, we see nothing to be gained and much to be lost in accommodating inflationary pressures." he added.
